name: Minchiate
description: Minchiate (also known as Germini or Gallerini) is a historic Italian trick-taking game played with a unique 97-card Tarot deck. Invented in Florence in the 16th century, it was once one of the most popular games in Italy. The game features complex scoring for 'versicole' (card combinations) and a unique 'Fola' system where players can exchange cards before play.

history.origins: Minchiate was invented in Florence in the 16th century. The name comes from 'sminchiare' meaning 'to play a high trump', though some incorrectly associate it with vulgar meanings. The alternative name 'Germini' derives from Gemini (trump 35).
timeline: 17th Century: Spreads to Rome, Sicily, and Genoa
18th-19th Century: Highly popular and respected game throughout Italy
1930s: Effectively dies out as last card manufacturer stops production
Late 20th Century: Reproduction decks created for collectors
Present: Played by enthusiasts attempting to revive the game
history.cultural: Considered one of the most sophisticated card games of its era. Played by nobility and intellectuals. The complexity of the game reflected the cultural sophistication of Florence.
history.evolution: The game evolved from standard Tarocchi by adding 19 extra trumps (virtues, elements, zodiac signs) to create a 97-card deck.

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships, partners sitting opposite each other.
setup.deck: 97-card Minchiate deck: 40 trumps (numbered 1-40), four suits of 14 cards each (Cups, Coins, Swords, Batons), and the Fool (Matto). The top 5 trumps (Arie) are unnumbered: Trumpets (40), World (39), Sun (38), Moon (37), Star (36).
setup.dealing: 21 cards to each player in batches. The remaining 13 cards form the 'Fola' (talon).

rules.objective: Score points by capturing valuable cards, declaring 'versicole' (combinations), and winning the last trick.
rules.gameplay: Play is counter-clockwise. Must follow suit if possible. If unable, must play a trump if possible. Highest trump wins, or highest card of led suit. The Fool can be played to any trick and is retained by the player.
keyRules: 40 trumps with special ranking (Arie are highest)
Must follow suit, must trump if void
Fool can be played to any trick

strategy.basic: Remember the unusual trump structure (40 trumps!). Try to capture high trumps and Kings. Declare versicole when you have them.
strategy.intermediate: Use the Fola exchange wisely to improve your hand. Track which high cards have been played. Coordinate with partner to capture valuable cards.
strategy.advanced: Expert card counting is essential with 97 cards. Optimize versicole declarations. Use the Fool strategically to avoid playing valuable cards on losing tricks. Master the complex scoring to maximize points.
tips: The Arie (top 5 trumps) are extremely valuable - capture or protect them
Versicole scoring happens twice - at declaration and at end
The Fola exchange gives crucial information about unavailable cards
The Fool is invaluable for saving your high cards
